subject: Staggered GPU uplift ladder & price-protection options
messages:
From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@nebulaai.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@nebulaai.com
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + mid-term uplifts — pricing protection request

Olga,

Hope you’re well. We’re kicking off our renewal conversation for the Dedicated GPU pool (current commit: 120 A100-equivalent units). Over the next 12–18 months we expect to ramp usage — likely a mid-term uplift in two phases (roughly +20% in Q3, +25% in Q1 next year).

A few asks from our side so we can evaluate options quickly:
- Can Redwood provide a staggered/add-on pricing ladder for mid-term uplifts (we’d like predictable incremental unit price tiers rather than the full renewal rate)?
- Price protection window: is 12 months standard? We’d prefer something longer if feasible (to 18 months) for up to ~25% cumulative uplift.
- Throughput guarantee: we need guidance on SLOs you can commit to (p95 token latency / guaranteed throughput for 100k tokens/min sustained) and whether overflow is auto-bucketed to lower-cost variants.
- Any pro-rated credits for the downtime incident we saw in May (SR-7712) — that impacted a couple of customer-facing jobs. I attached the incident ticket reference in case you need it.

Can you share a short proposal (pricing bands, suggested commitment + top-up structure, and indicative SLA language) and a fast path to signature if we align? Our procurement is ready to move once we have terms.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Gupta
Head of Infrastructure
Nebula AI
[samir.gupta@nebulaai.com]

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@nebulaai.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 10:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + mid-term uplifts — pricing protection request

Samir — thanks for the clear asks. We can do a pragmatic path that balances your predictability needs and our capacity planning. High level:

- Staggered uplift ladder: banded top-up pricing in three tiers (0–15% / 15–30% / 30%+) relative to baseline commit. Each band has a fixed incremental unit price (we'll show numbers in the attachment).
- Price protection: standard is 12 months; we can offer 18 months for uplifted capacity up to 25% if Nebula takes a small minimum additional commit (or agrees to a blended rate).
- Throughput & overflow: we can include a throughput SLO for sustained throughput and an overflow policy that routes excess to compatible model variants (with explicit fallback latency targets).
- Incident credit: we’ll review SR-7712 and propose a one-time service credit as a good-faith gesture once we reconcile the impact.

I attached a short proposal (Nebula-Proposal-v1.pdf) with pricing bands, a sample amendment for price protection, and the proposed DocuSign flow for quick signature. If this looks directionally right I’ll loop in Marcus for the discount/margin review and Laura for contract language.

Next steps: please confirm the target uplift ladder you expect (timing and % by quarter) and I’ll get a v1.1 with adjusted numbers out today.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive — Dedicated
Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: Nebula-Proposal-v1.pdf (pdf)
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 10:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Renewal + mid-term uplifts — pricing protection request (internal)

Team — forwarding Nebula’s note. Key asks: staggered top-ups, price protection to 18 months for up to ~25% uplift, throughput SLO, and a request for pro-rated credit for SR-7712.

My propose/ask:
- Baseline commit: keep 120 units. Nebula willing to commit to 25 additional units (annualized) if we can offer 18-month price protection for up to +25% uplift.
- Suggested commercial structure: 15% blended discount on baseline commit, tiered top-up discounts (8% for band 1, 5% for band 2). If procurement asks to push protection to 18 months we should ask for a minimal incremental committed spend (they’re sticky) or accept a slightly lower discount.
- Incident credit: offer $5k service credit contingent on review (keeps deal moving).

Margin check: we can flex to 13–15% blended on baseline if Marcus signs off. Marcus — can you take a quick look at the attached v1 and give a margin-approved revision? I want to respond to Samir this afternoon.

Thx,
Olga

Attachment (internal): Nebula-Proposal-v1.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Renewal + mid-term uplifts — pricing protection request (internal)

Olga / Laura — saw this. Recommend the following, conservative but competitive:

- Baseline commit discount: 15% blended (keeps gross margin acceptable).
- Top-up ladder: 0–15% at 12% discount; 15–30% at 6% discount; >30% priced at list (encourages commit).
- Price protection: we can extend to 18 months for up to 25% uplift if Nebula signs a 12-month minimum extension on their baseline commit and accepts the 15% blended baseline.
- Throughput SLOs: include a 99th percentile routing/throughput guardrail and explicit overflow routing to compatible model variants (note: overflow will be billed at top-up rates).
- Incident credit: approve a $5,000 service credit (one-time) to expedite close.

I’ve updated the proposal (Nebula-Proposal-v1.1.pdf) with the numbers and a short finance note. If Olga sends this verbatim I’ll approve the concession.

-Marcus
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Gupta <samir.gupta@nebulaai.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nebulaai.com
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 14:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal + mid-term uplifts — pricing protection request

Thanks, Olga — appreciate the quick turnaround. The band structure looks good directionally. A couple asks before we proceed to signature:
1) Can you extend price-protection to 18 months (we prefer the longer window) for up to 25% cumulative uplift?
2) We’d ask that the $5k incident credit be applied up front on the first invoice (helps us get procurement sign-off).
3) Please send a DocuSign link once you have the updated proposal v1.1 (we will circulate internally).

If you can confirm (1) and (2) I’ll get procurement the DocuSign and try to close this week.

Best,
Samir

Attachment: SR-7712-incident-summary.pdf (pdf)
